'''Hettie Belle Ege''' (31 March 1861 – 19 November 1942) was an American professor of mathematics. From 1914 to 1916, she was the acting president of [[Mills College]].

== Early life ==
Ege was born in [[Erie, Illinois]] on 31 March 1861, the daughter of Joseph Arthur Ege and his second wife, Catherine Rebecca Reisch Ege. Her parents were both from Pennsylvania; her father died the year she was born, and her mother remarried in 1869.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/historyandgenea00egegoog|title=History and genealogy of the Ege family in the United States, 1738-1911|last=Ege|first=Thompson Prettyman|date=1911|publisher=Harrisburg, Pa., The Star Printing Company|others=Allen County Public Library Genealogy Center|pages=[https://archive.org/details/historyandgenea00egegoog/page/n114 98]}}</ref> She attended [[Western College for Women|Western College]] in [[Oxford, Ohio]], graduating in 1886; she later graduated from Mills College in 1903, with further studies at the [[University of Chicago]], the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]], and the [[University of California]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cGXPAAAAMAAJ&dq=Hettie+Belle+Ege&pg=PA11|title=Catalogue ...|last=College|first=Mills|date=1916|publisher=Frank Eastman, book and job printer.|pages=11, 12|language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Ege taught school in Ohio and Colorado as a young woman. From 1895 to 1930,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://cdnc.ucr.edu/?a=d&d=SCS19421121.1.8&srpos=2&e=-------en--20--1--txt-txIN-Hettie+Belle+Ege-------1|title=Mills College Professor Dies|date=November 21, 1942|work=Santa Cruz Sentinel|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=8|via=California Digital Newspaper Collection}}</ref> she was a professor of mathematics and Dean of Women at Mills College.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/36199067/hettie_belle_ege_1918/|title=War Work is Women's Mass Meeting Topic|date=June 11, 1918|work=Oakland Tribune|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=4|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She also coached the Mills College basketball team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oac.cdlib.org/ark:/13030/kt309nf1zc/?brand=oac4|title=Photograph of the Mills Seminary basketball team|website=Online Archive of California|language=en|access-date=2019-09-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://calisphere.org/item/ark:/13030/kt4000342x/|title=Calisphere: Photograph of the Mills Seminary basketball team|website=Calisphere|language=en|access-date=2019-09-21}}</ref> From 1914 to 1916, she was the college's acting president.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Gibbons|first=Vernette Lois|title=The Institution of the Zeta Chapter of California|date=1929|journal=The Phi Beta Kappa Key|volume=7|issue=4|pages=232–239|issn=2373-0331|jstor=42914185}}</ref> "Since Mills is to California what Wellesley is to the East," explained a California magazine in 1915, "it is most apparent that the leading spirit of the institution is a dominant figure in the educational activities of the state."<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Ege|first=Hettie B.|date=July 1915|title=Education for Young Women in California|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nMUVAQAAIAAJ&dq=Hettie+Ege&pg=PA391|journal=California's Magazine Quarterly|volume=1|pages=391–393; image 392}}</ref>

In 1918, she chaperoned a unit of 28 Mills students in the [[Woman's Land Army of America|Woman's Land Army]], providing ranch labor during wartime shortages.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/36200060/hettie_belle_ege_1918/|title=Mills Girls Organize for Ranch Labor|date=May 19, 1918|work=Oakland Tribune|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=44|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> In 1920, the college marked her twenty-five years at Mills with a presentation and convocation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/36199580/hettie_belle_ege_1920/|title=Mills College Founders Day Rites Today|date=October 8, 1920|work=The San Francisco Examiner|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=2|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/36199742/hettie_belle_ege_1920/|title=Mills College Celebrates Founders' Day, Honors Dean|date=October 8, 1920|work=Oakland Tribune|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=11|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> At the festivities marking the school's founder's centennial in 1925, Ege received an honorary doctorate.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/36199439/hettie_berlle_ege_1925/|title=Mills Observes its Centennial|date=October 2, 1925|work=Oakland Tribune|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=1|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

After her retirement in 1930,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/36199847/hettie_belle_ege_1930/|title=Mills College Dean to Retire|date=June 11, 1930|work=Oakland Tribune|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=16|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> she spent some time in [[Cambridge]], in England.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/36199156/hettie_belle_ege_1931/|title=Mills College Dean Aids Fund|date=January 26, 1931|work=Oakland Tribune|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=5|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She was a regular guest at Mills College events<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/36198874/hettie_belle_ege_1936/|title=Miss Ege Will Be Entertained|date=November 15, 1936|work=Oakland Tribune|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=38|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> and alumnae gatherings: in 1933 she was honored as the college's dean emerita, alongside president [[Aurelia Henry Reinhardt]] and physician [[Mariana Bertola]], at an annual breakfast of the Mills Club of San Francisco.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://cdnc.ucr.edu/?a=d&d=OT19330414.1.21&e=-------en--20--1--txt-txIN--------1|title=Untitled society item|date=April 14, 1933|work=Oakland Tribune|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=21|via=California Digital Newspaper Collection}}</ref>

== Death ==
Ege died November 19, 1942, aged 81 years, in [[Oakland, California]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/36198634/hettie_belle_ege_1942/|title=Hettie Belle Ege|date=November 30, 1942|work=The Dispatch|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=17|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/36199921/obituary_for_reinhardt_hettie_aged_65/|title=Hettie Ege, Dean Emeritus of Mills, Dies in Sleep|date=November 20, 1942|work=Oakland Tribune|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=25|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Her grave is on the campus of Mills College, and there is a dormitory named for Ege at Mills.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://inside.mills.edu/student-life/housing/berkeley.php|title=Housing for UC Berkeley Students|website=Housing {{!}} Inside Mills|access-date=2019-09-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/36198733/hettie_belle_ege_1970/|title=Mills Halls Dedication Rites Slated|date=October 25, 1970|work=Oakland Tribune|access-date=September 21, 2019|page=17|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>
